narrative:
Trilobites were extinct arthropods with hard exoskeletons that dominated Earth's ancient oceans [[3]]. These segmented, multilimbed creatures were roughly bug-like in appearance and crawled along the seafloor [[1]][[2]]. When threatened, they could roll up defensively like modern woodlice [[2]].

Trilobites first appeared abundantly during the Cambrian Period, which spanned from 541 to 485 million years ago, at a time when Earth's atmospheric and ocean oxygen levels were approximately 50% of modern levels and deep ocean waters remained oxygen-free [[1]]. They mobbed the oceans hundreds of millions of years before dinosaurs and mammals lived on land [[3]]. During the Cambrian, trilobites were the dominant animal form, comprising some 75% of all fossil species discovered in rocks from this period [[1]].

As extinct arthropods, trilobites represent a crucial chapter in the history of life on Earth, demonstrating the early success of animals with segmented bodies and hard protective exoskeletons in ancient marine environments [[1]][[3]].
